text: Lilia Mann hasn't lost a ranked game since her first year. People have stopped keeping count.
The Commons gets cold showers because the school wants you to duel your way out. (The boiler is simply broken; nobody budgeted for it.)
There's a secret fifth rarity above Spectral and the teachers all have one.
Umbra House is haunted. A whole class vanished. (Four students were sent home; one professor did not come back.)
Chuck Kaboom has never once played the same deck twice in an exhibition. He says he plays 'whoever turns up'.
Chuck is senile and the board keeps him around as a mascot.
A real Alpha common sold on the mainland last year for more than a Commons kid's whole tuition.
Willas Tann is only on the Battle Team because he's sleeping with the captain. (He's on it because she wants him there; he also trains harder than anyone.)
Rana Marika is the only student in the school's history held back a year without failing a single class.
The fortune teller at the night market has been there longer than the market. Ask anyone's grandmother.
Old Silas pulled the Founder off the north shore half dead, fifty years back. Neither of them will tell it the same way twice.
Ashton Beaumont-Lyle's roses are grown in a private greenhouse his father had shipped in. (He buys them at the boutique, on account.)
The Hale guy in Bungalow 5 is a treasure hunter and there's gold in the ruins. (He is hunting; it isn't gold.)
The girl with the green hair asked for the Commons. On purpose. Who does that?
Professor Santángel threw the world final. (He lost it fairly and has never forgiven himself.)
The fourteen-year-old in Spectral is already ranked above half the third-years.
Josie at the Mulligan used to wear a smoke-grey collar up at the school. Don't bring it up.
The Archive's Alpha cards are replicas; the real ones are in a bank in Zurich.
'Inya Bell' is Inya Kaboom. The Founder's granddaughter has been eating Commons rice for three weeks.
Inya's bracket was rigged for her. (She went out in the semi-final to Georgie.)
Some nights there's a lantern on the jungle trail. It's the keeper walking his rounds. (He is walking after someone.)
BREAKING: something came down on the north slope at ten past two. The Top Deck has drone footage of a crater 'the size of the pool'. (It is forty metres across.)
{H:full} touched the meteor. ({H:He} reached it. What touched what is another matter.)
Crater glass sells for 50 cr a chip in town. Tomi has chips. (They're from a broken bottle.)
It was a satellite and the cordon is because of the fuel.
The harbour gulls have moved to the breakwater. Fishermen say the catch off the south cove is down to nothing.
{H:ladder} has not dropped a ranked game since the meteor. Chat is calling it 'crater brain'.
{H}'s got promo cards from a set that isn't out yet. {H:His} uncle works at Kaboom. ({H:He} has no such uncle.)
Brant Kessler took something. Pills. That's why they're calling it a seizure.
The Dome 3 recorder 'malfunctioned' on the night of the Kessler incident. (It worked perfectly. It recorded silence.)
The nurse hasn't left the infirmary in four days.
That's two. The Top Deck has been asked not to say 'two'.
It's the meteor dust. Don't drink from the north streams.
Every one of them played a game the night before. Tomi has it in a ledger and he's stopped laughing about it.
Kaboom Entertainment has sent a board member to 'support the school through a difficult term'. He brought a prize fund. (He brought a great deal more than that.)
The suits at the inn pay for everything in cash and have asked three different people about the north slope.
Curfew is because there's an animal loose. Something that came out of the crater.
North Crown's captain bowed to Lilia Mann after losing. Chat lost its mind.
Someone broke into the Archive. (Someone walked in with a professor's card.)
Captain Stroud turned away paying cargo. Crates that sweat.
They only take people who deserve it. Bullies, sharks, snitches. (They take whoever sits down.)
{H:last} won {H:his} Promotion Duel in six turns and turned down Rare Hall. Quote: 'I have a {H:mate}.' Chat thinks it's adorable.
A third of the Spectral upper years didn't come back from break.
The Battle Team has 'closed practice for tactical reasons'. (They are frightened.)
Kenji Watanabe. In the dome. With his headphones still on.
The ones in the ward wake up if you take them off the island. A cousin of a cousin saw it.
The Chancellor is 'considering her position'. (The board is considering it for her.)
Lilia Mann sat across from him all night. She didn't cry. Somebody said that was worse.
The Founder's turning seventy-five and they say he'll announce a new set at the festival. (He has something to announce. It is not a set.)
The Top Deck's last broadcast under this management: there is a fence going up around the ruins, and the name on the fence is not the school's.
One of the first-years got in without a placement rank. Somebody's daughter. (Somebody's daughter, yes. Not with somebody's permission.)
The pale one in the long coat from Bungalow 6 did time. Or his brother did. Or he says his brother did.
The mail window knows who got a parcel before they do. Ask nicely and she'll tell you that much, and nothing else.
The girl with the parasol sat on the same bench from lunch till dark and didn't notice.
There's a first-year who was number two to the Wildcard kid online for two years and has taken it personally.
The tall blonde from the far north doesn't drink. (She had not started yet.)
You can't take the little prodigy from the Tower anywhere without signing a book. (True. The warden is not as fierce as she sounds.)
Somebody in Bungalow 6 owns a crowbar. Tomi isn't saying who. Tomi would like it known he's on good terms with them.
The green-haired one made Baylee Halvorsen cry over a sausage. Baylee. Cry.
Hologram tech on this island is twenty years behind because the Founder likes it that way. (It is as good as it can be made — without something nobody is supposed to use.)
The ladder registrar can be talked into rounding a result. (Nobody has ever managed it, and three people have tried.)
The Commons steward has asked for a new boiler thirty-one times. (He has. Nobody at the school will say where the money went.)
The goth from Bungalow 4 made top 8 at the Cup. The goth. Three boys have had to rethink things.
A boy in a cowboy hat tried to climb the rope bridge from underneath. The Hale lad pulled him off by the belt.
The arena's stage manager used to be famous for something and won't say what. (He was nine.)
Old print-works people used to get a cough. Ask at the harbour who's left of the ink room. (Two. Neither will say much.)
Someone's leaving money under doors on the Commons. Guilt, probably. (Something like it.)
The quiet kid in the black coat put a curse on Brant Kessler. He as good as said so.
Post for the mainland isn't going straight to the ferry any more. It goes up the hill first.
The Commons blacked out because the girl with the goggles is building a hologram you can touch. She says it nearly works.
The suit has been to see the hologram professor three times this month. The professor looks worse each time.
Helical got caught in the Archive stealing first prints. (She was reading a ledger.)
The tutor desk girl is entered for the Island Open, and she's stopped taking bookings for that week.
